# Terms & Conditions

Last updated · 17 August 2026

## 01 · About the competition

UNSW Battlecode is a programming competition organised by the UNSW Competitive Programming and Mathematics
Society ("we", "us"). By signing up or participating you accept these terms.

## 02 · Eligibility

The competition ladder is open to everyone. The Grand Final and its associated prizes are open only to
participants who are either currently enrolled at a university or high school in the Asia-Pacific region, or
citizens of one of the countries or territories listed below currently enrolled at a university or high
school outside the region, and every member of a team must meet this criterion for the team to be eligible.
We may ask for proof of enrolment, citizenship, or age at any time. The top 10 eligible teams from the
Qualifier are invited to the Grand Final; we may invite more at our discretion. Participants under 18 need
the consent of a parent or guardian. Any finalist team consisting of any members under 18 must have at least
one parent or guardian of an underage member present at the Grand Final. At most two high school teams will
be invited to the Grand Final, selected by qualifier ranking, with remaining places passing to the next
eligible teams. A high school team is any team with a member currently enrolled at a high school; this cap
is about enrolment, not age. We reserve the right to disqualify any team or participant that does not meet
these eligibility requirements, and our decisions are final.

For prize eligibility, the Asia-Pacific region means the following countries and territories:

- Australia
- Bangladesh
- Bhutan
- Brunei

If your country or territory is not listed, contact us and we will confirm your eligibility.

## 03 · Accounts

The details you register with must be accurate, and each person may hold only one account. You are
responsible for keeping your account credentials secure and for anything done through your account.

## 04 · Teams

Teams have between 1 and 4 members, and each person may be in only one team at a time. Declarations you make
at registration, such as your institution and country, affect eligibility for finals and prizes. False
declarations may lead to disqualification.

## 05 · Bot submissions and intellectual property

You keep ownership of the code you submit. You grant us a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to execute,
store, and display your submissions for the purposes of running the competition, including replays and
broadcasting matches. Submissions must be your team's own work, must not infringe anyone else's rights, and
must not contain malicious code.

## 06 · Fair play

Bots run in a sandboxed environment with resource limits that depend on the language used. Attempting to
circumvent the sandbox, access the network, interfere with other teams, or exploit the platform will lead to
disqualification. Our decisions on rule breaches and results are final.

## 07 · Prizes

Prizes are awarded at our discretion and split equally between team members unless the team agrees
otherwise; hardware awards are one per team member. Awards for a specific criterion, such as the fastest
algorithm or the top-ranked team of first-year students, stack with each other and with any placing. Winners
and finalists may be asked to provide additional information for prize fulfilment, including details needed
to arrange travel to the Grand Final in Sydney.

A finalist team that cannot attend the Grand Final because of visa issues may compete remotely and remains
eligible for prizes. We will provide a letter of invitation to support visa applications, but we cannot
guarantee that a visa is granted in time.

The Sprint tournament is open to entrants worldwide, but we cannot award Sprint prize money to participants
residing in the following countries, and a team with any such member is not eligible for the Sprint prize:

- Afghanistan
- Belarus
- Cuba
- Iran
- North Korea
- Russia
- Syria

## 08 · Liability

The platform and competition are provided as is. We do not guarantee uptime, and to the extent permitted by
law we are not liable for losses arising from your participation.

## 09 · Changes

We may update these terms. Material changes will be announced on this site or on our Discord server.

## 10 · Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of New South Wales, Australia.
